facts.statement: The holotype specimen IGM 100/1321 includes the back of the skull, lower jaws, neck vertebrae, front limb parts, and bony armor plates.
facts.quote: The holotype of Z. shepardi is IGM 100/1321, consisting of the posterior region of the skull and lower jaws in articulation with cervical vertebrae, forelimb elements and osteoderms.

facts.statement: Its skull was relatively wide with the upper openings completely closed by surrounding skull bones, a trait shared with other gobiosuchids.
facts.quote: The skull was relatively wide, with the upper temporal fenestrae of the skull being completely closed off by the surrounding squamosal and parietal bones (characteristic of Gobiosuchids).

facts.statement: It had highly developed bony armor plates, with four rows of dorsal plates fused to each other, each featuring a sharp spike and rough ridges.
facts.quote: It possessed highly developed osteoderms, with 4 rows of dorsal osteoderms laterally sutured to each other, each one with a sharp, pronounced spike and several rugose ridges.

facts.statement: Its neck armor plates were likely fused to the back plates to form a complete concentric ring of armor around the neck, torso, and tail.
facts.quote: The cervical ventral osteoderms were disarticulated, but these were likely sutured laterally with the dorsal osteoderms to complete a concentric

facts.statement: Its front limbs were long and slender, though only an incomplete set is preserved in the fossil record.
facts.quote: The holotype preserves an incomplete forelimb, these were long and gracile.

facts.statement: Researchers classified it as the closest relative to Gobiosuchus kielanae, sharing 14 key skull features that define the family Gobiosuchidae.
facts.quote: Pol and Norell (2004) found Zaraasuchus shepardi to be the sister taxon of Gobiosuchus kielanae, united by 14 synapomorphies, primarily from the skull, forming the family Gobiosuchidae.

facts.statement: It lived during the Campanian stage of the Late Cretaceous, between 83.6 and 72.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Campanian (83.6 to 72.2 million years ago)

facts.statement: Its long and slender front limbs suggest it may have been adapted for a terrestrial lifestyle rather than swimming.
facts.quote: The holotype preserves an incomplete forelimb, these were long and gracile.

rejected.statement: Zaraasuchus is a gobiosuchid crocodyliform described in 2004 by Diego Pol and Mark Norell. It was found in the Red Beds of Zos Canyon, in the Gobi Desert of Mongolia, thus making it Late Cretaceous in age. The type species is Z. shepardi, honouring Dr. Richard Shepard.
